title: Cybersecurity Daily Briefing
description: Actively exploited vulnerabilities, major incidents, and threat trends relevant to enterprise and federal networks.
readFirst: Covers Oct. 23–26. The patching priority is two CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities additions from Oct. 23, both with a catalog due date of Oct. 26: Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator CVE-2026-114625, and Collabora Online's built-in CODE Server CVE-2026-110447. CISA revised the php2shell alert on Oct. 23 and still said it had not observed successful exploitation as of publication. No CISA alert was posted for Oct. 24, Oct. 25, or Oct. 26. The Oct. 22 Siemens industrial advisory and the Oct. 21 OpenAI Daybreak note were dropped so this page does not keep an old CVE backlog. No new public update on the DMDC personnel breach was found.

items.headline: CISA put the exploited VeloCloud Orchestrator bug on the KEV list, due Oct. 26
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-114625 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct. 23, and the catalog sets a due date of Oct. 26. Arista's Oct. 22 advisory scores the on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator SQL injection at 9.9 and says any authenticated user, including Enterprise Read Only, can become a local superuser operator. Arista says the flaw is being exploited, names 74.82.197.86 and 38.54.50.151 as addresses seen in the attacks, and gives the on-premises fixes as VCO 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10, and 6.4.2.12 and later. Hosted and Dedicated orchestrators are already patched, and Gateway and Edge are not affected.

items.headline: CISA adds an exploited Collabora CODE Server bug, with a catalog due date of Oct. 26
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-110447 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct. 23, based on evidence of active exploitation, and the catalog sets a due date of Oct. 26. Collabora's advisory says it is an unauthenticated command injection in proxy.php in the Nextcloud app Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server before 26.4.303, and that it works only while the built-in server is not running, such as after a restart, upgrade, or crash. Collabora says disabling the app is not enough: upgrade to 26.4.303 or later, or remove it. Standalone Collabora Online servers are not affected, and Collabora says this is not CVE-2025-66208.

items.headline: CISA revises the php2shell alert and still says it has not seen successful exploitation
items.summary: CISA revised its php2shell alert on Oct. 23, adding a SIGMA detection rule and links to partner advisories, and repeated the fix: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35. CISA said the bugs allow unauthenticated remote code execution on PHP that serves web requests, that Apache with mod_php is the configuration PHP considers highest risk, and that it had not observed successful exploitation in the wild as of publication. Cisco's advisory, updated the same day, lists Ultra-Reliable Wireless Backhaul, Expressway, and Duo Access Gateway as affected, says the backhaul bug requires an administrator, and says products not on the list are not affected, including Secure Firewall ASA, Management Center, and Threat Defense. Cisco PSIRT said it is not aware of malicious use of these flaws.

items.headline: Microsoft says Storm-0940 used an AI pentest framework in the ConnectWise compromise
items.summary: Microsoft said Oct. 21 that Storm-0940, which it describes as a China-state-aligned actor, used the open-source agentic penetration-testing framework ARTEX and was responsible for the ConnectWise multi-tenant application compromise. After that access, Microsoft said, the actor used ARTEX to attempt sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants at 2,900 attempts per minute, and in multiple cases reached privileged cloud access in under three hours. Microsoft said the activity did not come from a flaw in Microsoft's own products, and that an affected application or a successful sign-in does not by itself mean customer data was taken. Its guidance is to keep the affected ConnectWise application connections disabled until ConnectWise publishes restoration instructions, and to review activity from at least Oct. 15.

items.headline: SafePay advisory: about 600 victims, initial access through edge devices and stolen passwords
items.summary: CISA, the FBI, the Secret Service and international partners released a StopRansomware advisory on SafePay dated Oct. 20. A CISA news release the next day says the group has hit about 600 victims across the Americas, Europe and Australia and is one of the most active ransomware groups of 2026. Actors steal or guess passwords, use phishing, and exploit known vulnerabilities on internet-facing devices, often arriving through VPN, then create or take over accounts, move with legitimate admin tools, disable backups, steal data and encrypt systems. Listed bugs include CVE-2020-3259, CVE-2023-20269, CVE-2023-27532, CVE-2024-40711 and CVE-2024-40766, and CISA's ask is to patch edge devices, require multifactor authentication, restrict admin tools, segment networks and keep offline backups that have been restored in a test.

items.headline: Cisco: eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys can be brute-forced, and firewalls are still under review
items.summary: Cisco's informational advisory, first published Oct. 23 and updated Oct. 24, says a researcher showed that private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates can be brute-forced in seconds because of an error in an April 2025 key ceremony, and that anyone with those keys can issue fraudulent TLS certificates for any domain. Cisco says two of the eight are code-signing CAs, and that all eight were cross-signed by Sectigo's AAA Certificate Services root in May 2025. Cisco PSIRT said it is not aware of malicious use. Secure Firewall Management Center has a remediation article, while Secure Firewall ASA, Threat Defense, and Identity Services Engine were still under investigation in the Oct. 24 update.
